title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Alternative Methods - Sole Source
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios is the most valid justification for a Sole Source procurement?
options: The requested vendor offers a steep, limited-time discount
The requested software is highly preferred by the IT department
The requested item is patented and manufactured by only one vendor who has no authorized resellers
The current vendor is locally owned and heavily supports the community
questions.explain: A sole source procurement is strictly used when a single vendor is the ONLY source that exists in the market capable of meeting the requirement, such as with exclusive patents or original equipment manufacturer (OEM) restrictions.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following is required before an agency can officially award a sole source contract?
options: A formal negotiation with at least three vendors
A detailed written justification documenting market research proving no other sources exist
Approval from a minimum of three competing contractors
An independent financial audit of the chosen vendor
questions.explain: Sole source procurements circumvent the standard competitive process and legally require robust, written justification and market research to prove only one viable vendor exists.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A department submits a sole source request stating, 'Vendor X is the only vendor we trust based on 10 years of successful past performance.' How should the buyer respond?
options: Approve it, as past performance guarantees future success
Reject it, because 'trust' and past history do not prove Vendor X is the only source in the marketplace
Approve it, but classify it as an emergency
Reject it, but process it as a Qualification-Based Selection
questions.explain: A sole source must be justified by market reality (i.e., only one supplier exists for a required good or service), not by mere preference, comfort, or past relationship with the vendor.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency is purchasing an upgrade for its proprietary dispatch software. The original software developer is the only entity with the source code and legal right to modify it. This procurement should be classified as a:
options: Sole Source
Single Source
Pilot Program
QBS
questions.explain: Because only the original developer holds the proprietary rights and access to the source code, no other vendor could legally or technically fulfill the requirement, making it a true sole source.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: To properly vet a Sole Source request, an agency will often publicly post a 'Notice of Intent to Sole Source.' What is the primary reason for this?
options: To satisfy public relations requirements
To give the selected vendor a timeline for delivery
To allow other potential vendors the opportunity to prove they can also provide the good/service, thus verifying if competition truly exists
To waive the agency's terms and conditions
questions.explain: A Notice of Intent allows the market to challenge the sole source claim. If another vendor demonstrates they can meet the need, the agency must cancel the sole source and issue a competitive solicitation.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A buyer is reviewing a sole source request for a replacement part. The department states the manufacturer will void the warranty of the entire million-dollar machine if an aftermarket part is used. How does this impact the sourcing method?
options: It prevents a sole source because warranties are negotiable
It provides a valid basis for a sole source or single source to OEM parts to preserve the valuable warranty
The buyer must issue an IFB and inform bidders they assume warranty risk
The buyer must convert the purchase to an emergency
questions.explain: Preserving a critical warranty by adhering strictly to Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts is a recognized and valid justification for waiving full and open competition via a sole/single source.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which condition below frequently leads to a legitimate sole source procurement?
options: The item is heavily advertised by a single distributor
The commodity is a highly traded agricultural product
The procurement requires compatibility with existing proprietary intellectual property
The department director has an existing relationship with a vendor
questions.explain: Proprietary intellectual property, such as copyrighted materials or closed-architecture software interfaces, physically restricts other vendors from fulfilling the need, justifying a sole source.
